clue.text: Incomplete fondness?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: the state of being incomplete

blocks.note: first meaning: the condition of being only in part
second meaning: a liking or bias towards something

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests half-hearted love; the question mark flags that the answer's two senses are being split.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a partiality for something means a particular liking, and the word also names the state of being partial or unfinished.

clue.text: Vain display from French president? Not half!

indicators.note: only half of the word survives, the rest is dropped

blocks.note: Georges Pompidou was President of France 1969-74

explanation.surface: A sneer at a French leader's showing off, with the British exclamation 'Not half!' meaning 'and how!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it keeps only the first four of eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is ostentatious ceremony or splendour, an empty show of grandeur.

clue.text: This king contracted a detective in America

definitions.note: a description of the name: shortened, it is US slang for a private eye

blocks.note: first meaning: the name of three English kings
second meaning: its pet form is the American word for a detective

explanation.walkthrough: Dick is the pet form of the name, and a dick is American slang for a detective; 'contracted' means shortened, not hired.
explanation.definitionFit: England had three kings of this name, so it names a royal.

clue.text: It could be rent I switched

blocks.clueFragment: It could be rent I switched
blocks.note: surface reading: a remark about payment being swapped
setter's reading: split the answer after five letters; those five letters, once changed, could become rent I

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as INTER + CHANGED, an instruction to rearrange INTER, and one result is RENT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Things interchanged have been swapped with each other, which is what switched means.

clue.text: Cross area of Eastern France

blocks.note: first meaning: the two-barred cross of this name, emblem of the Free French
second meaning: the region around Nancy and Metz

explanation.surface: An annoyed part of eastern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the Cross of Lorraine, a cross with two bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The region gives its name to a heraldic cross, so the word fills both 'Cross of ...' and the place.

clue.text: Informant who makes votes count

blocks.note: first meaning: one who tells
second meaning: an official who counts votes, as in Parliament

explanation.surface: A whistleblower ensures every ballot matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller is someone who tells, and also the counter of votes in a division or ballot.

clue.text: Serve food in interval

blocks.note: first meaning: to attend tables, as a waiter does
second meaning

explanation.surface: Food is served during the interval at a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiters wait at table, serving meals; a wait is also a stretch of time spent before something happens.

clue.text: One barely recognizable as human being?

blocks.note: first meaning: a member of a sect known for going naked
second meaning: any descendant of the first man in Genesis

explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' looks like 'hardly', but means 'in the nude': the Adamites were a sect who worshipped naked, as Adam did before the Fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers a member of that nudist sect and any person descended from the first man of Genesis.

clue.text: Short trains I moved onto railway

indicators.note: the single letter is shifted to a new spot within the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
read as on + to: the word to, placed on what follows in this down entry
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A brief note about rearranging carriages on a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I moved' shifts only the one letter rather than mixing the whole word; 'onto' splits as on + to, putting the little word on top of the railway in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transitory lasts only briefly, so it is short-lived.

clue.text: He learnt ambition from so-called Tortoise

definitions.text: He learnt ambition from so-called Tortoise

blocks.clueFragment: He learnt ambition from so-called Tortoise
blocks.note: surface reading: a pupil taught to be ambitious by a teacher with a nickname
setter's reading: in Alice in Wonderland the schoolmaster was called Tortoise 'because he taught us', and Ambition was one of the lessons

explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland the Mock Turtle describes his sea school, where an old turtle nicknamed Tortoise taught Ambition, Distraction, Uglification and Derision.
explanation.definitionFit: The character from Carroll's book is the pupil who studied those comic arithmetic branches under the old master.

clue.text: A shock reverse for ruler

indicators.note: a reverse sends things backwards, so the letters before it are read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: A sudden setback comes as a nasty surprise for a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A raja is an Indian king or prince, so the title names a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Chance incident for 1 dn's musical associate

blocks.note: first meaning: an event or happening
second meaning: the partner of 1 down in Elgar's Pomp and ... marches

explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is POMP; Elgar's marches pair it with this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A circumstance is an incident or fact of a situation, and the word follows Pomp in Elgar's title.

clue.text: Just average

blocks.note: first meaning: equitable, even-handed
second meaning: middling, so-so

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just average' reads as 'merely ordinary', but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair decision is an equitable one, and a fair performance is only moderately good.

clue.text: Pleasant features for chaps in first-class matches

indicators.note: chaps placed in the first-class pair means they sit inside it

blocks.note: chaps are men
A1 means first-class, with the 1 written as the letter I
ties are cup matches

explanation.surface: Nice facilities laid on for the men playing in top-level games.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is the old shipping register's top grade, so first-class; in British football a cup tie is a knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are agreeable facilities or attractions of a place, the things that make it pleasant.

clue.text: Birds cut with beaks

blocks.note: to cross is to cut across
a bird's bill is its beak

explanation.surface: Birds injured by pecking beaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossbills are finches whose bill tips cross over, used for prising seeds from cones.

clue.text: Opposite to green, mishit golf shot gets birdie

blocks.note: red is set against green, as on traffic lights
a shank is a golf shot struck off the club's heel

explanation.surface: On the putting surface, a duffed shot still ends with a birdie for a golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' and 'birdie' both pose as golf terms; birdie here simply means a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The redshank is a wading bird with red legs, so it is a bird in the playful diminutive.

clue.text: Take edible mushroom in turn

indicators.note: the mushroom placed in the turn means it goes inside that word

blocks.note: the cep is the edible porcini mushroom
a turn is a variety act

explanation.surface: Eat a mushroom when it is offered to you in your turn.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn is a performer's spot on a variety bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something offered is to accept it, as in taking or accepting a gift.

clue.text: Take off below the wind here?

definitions.text: Take off below the wind here?

indicators.note: in a down entry, below puts the first item under the second

blocks.note: air, a breeze
to strip is to take off clothes

explanation.surface: Planes lift off into the wind at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: aircraft take off into the wind from one.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: Parting words from wise man ere midnight

indicators.note: ere means before, so the wise man comes first in the line

blocks.note: Solon was the wise lawgiver of ancient Athens
read as mid-night: the central letter of the word night

explanation.surface: A sage says his goodbyes just before twelve o'clock at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' looks like a single time of day; split it as mid + night.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal farewell, the words spoken on parting.

clue.text: Flower-girl carries article in flexible way

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside

blocks.note: Lily is both a flower and a girl's name
the definite article

explanation.surface: A girl selling flowers carries an item with supple grace.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithely means with a supple, nimble grace, so in a flexible or limber way.

clue.text: Thinly cover a heavenly body to get one?

definitions.text: Thinly cover a heavenly body to get one?

blocks.note: to film is to coat with a thin layer
a star is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: A recipe for a celebrity: give some heavenly body a thin coating.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a 'heavenly body' is also a glamorous figure, and putting one on film makes a star.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie celebrity is a star of cinema, and the clue's wordplay doubles as the way one is made.

clue.text: Beef for champions

blocks.note: first meaning: a lean joint cut from the top of the leg
second meaning: the leading team

explanation.surface: A meal of beef for the winners.
explanation.walkthrough: Topside is a British cut of beef for roasting; a side is a team.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint is a standard British cut, and a top side is the best team in a league.

clue.text: Place for Merchant of Venice in trial, too

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the two words

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice has a trial scene and a Venetian setting too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is Venice's commercial district, where Shylock asks 'What news on the Rialto?'

clue.text: Current sources for violent offences

blocks.note: first meaning: cells that supply electric current
second meaning: in law, assaults involving physical contact

explanation.surface: The origins of today's rise in violent crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day'; it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical cells produce current, and battery is the legal term for an unlawful physical attack.

clue.text: Losing Gaza at the start. Egypt changed character

indicators.note: losing something means it drops out of the word that follows
the start of a word is its opening letter
changed means rearranged into a different order

blocks.note: the opening letter of Gaza
taken as written

explanation.surface: Losing Gaza first changed the character of Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: Egypt loses its G, and the four letters left are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Type and character are both used for a printed letter, and also for a kind or nature.

clue.text: Defeat one's optimal effort

blocks.note: first meaning: to get the better of
second meaning

explanation.surface: Losing despite giving it everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat them, and your best is the most you can manage.

clue.text: Fabricated musical setting for verse

blocks.note: first meaning: told untruths
second meaning: a German art song setting a poem

explanation.surface: Someone invented a tune to go with a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Lied, past tense of lie, means made things up; a Lied is a German song such as Schubert's settings of poems.

clue.text: A sort of Italian biscuit

blocks.note: first meaning: a native of Florence
second meaning: a thin nut-and-fruit cookie coated with chocolate

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase, an Italian biscuit, but splits after 'Italian'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Florence is a Florentine, and the same name belongs to a lacy biscuit of nuts and candied fruit.

clue.text: One of a group of islands or scattered keys

definitions.text: One of a group of islands

indicators.note: scattered things are thrown about out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Keys, low islands, are scattered across the sea in a group.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is the largest of Scotland's Inner Hebrides; 'keys' as low islands is a tempting false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye belongs to the Inner Hebrides archipelago off western Scotland.

clue.text: Sounds like commendation for all the crew

indicators.note: says the answer is pronounced like the word that follows

blocks.note: a compliment is a word of praise

explanation.surface: The whole crew is praised.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's complement is its full number of crew needed to man it.
